The goodness, magnitude, and right parts—or rather, the warnings to the artist—are such that certain principles reach their end without their primary principles which are in the center. Indeed, the primary ends are of such an hour as the primary ones, and greater than the secondary ones, as must be explored in the long parts; we do not care for this now, as it does not pertain to the mode of exploration of this art. It must be observed that this principle exists in this art so that the artist may consider what it is and investigate it, even without the mastery of this Figure B, in which one can truly perform wonders in the work of stone-making <note>original: "lapidifico"</note>. **r s t v x y z** are the principles placed in this Figure B, and through these, the artist understands that they are all sensible things from which the origin and the body arise. That which behaves as material <note>original: "materia"</note> is distinct from that which is formal <note>original: "formali"</note>. Those which are in the material are **b t v y**, which represent the "two" and the "four" for the artist's plan. Those which are formal are **x y z h**. Finally, the artist should consider **b r v y z** and know from which things the material or quicksilver <term>Quicksilver: Mercury, considered the "mother" of all metals in alchemy</term> is produced, which must be fixed so that it becomes **q r s t v x y z**. # The Vegetable Earth

The **Vegetable Earth** <note>Latin: *Terra vegetabilis*; a term for the primary matter of the alchemist's work</note> is what the artist must understand. When you are in this state, you must not let the body be destroyed. Then, as a true artist, you must possess the skill and habit by which our grain is directed in this state. It remains there until its action and reason are fulfilled, leading to the birth of the body. During the time it takes to complete this, you must not allow the fire to cease. At that time, leave it to digest until it is fully cooked. When it is digested, you will find in that moment a round mass, perfect in every way as it should be. You shall take it and place it in a clean vessel, and put it in the furnace of rotation <note>A furnace designed to maintain a constant, circulating heat</note>, which is its bath. Let it remain there for six days, administering the fire successively in such a way that where the vessel stands, you could still bear to hold your hand there. You shall observe the opportune time, for one part of this weight will suffice over two thousand parts. It is multiplied by its own likeness in these things. <insert>See the second part regarding the weight in the first number.</insert>

There is also another thing to know regarding the time and the method. It is this: take one pound during the ministry, and of **Gold** <note>Original uses the symbol ☉ for Sol/Gold</note> two **ounces** <note>Original uses the symbol ℥</note>, or two and a half ounces, according to the proportion of the powders. The deposition of the weights is five drams for a space of 30 days. All that which is in the melting, you should apply the fire and regulate it without ceasing, always governing the colors according to more or less, until you see one round body with redness. And if it is of the white, it will be in the whiteness of the metal. The artist must note that the colors differ in the generation of these moments. For

<column-break/>

the color of the moment which is red is conditioned as stated above. And the color in the moment of the white is conditioned by another condition. For the first time is to see a certain redness according to the letter K, which is the sign of the first guidance. It is like a true mixture with a splendid redness. The third time is the sign of the fixation of the moment, and it is white and splendid. Another time is the sign of the fixation of the soul in the body, and it is a shining white mixed into the metallic color. In this color, place the **Cinnabar** <note>Latin: *zinapri*; mercury sulfide, used here as a reagent or metaphor for the red stage</note> of the mother, from which one part of weight over so many thousands can multiply its strength from 3 to 7000. And of this, it performs as above. I estimate that in the whole work of stone-making <note>Latin: *lapidisico*</note> without a philosopher, there was a certain time when the matter arises into its own nature. This heat is friendly when it carries the matter, though sometimes it is slow because of the heat of the furnace. As is seen in the womb, where sometimes the birth occurs at seven months, and sometimes at nine. For these things happen in the mines of the universe where the heat is valid, intense, and strong, and in others where the heat is remiss and not vigorous. However, the color is your sign in the mastery of all works, and by it, you can regulate yourself. When you see the whole thing liquefied and mixed, and the color of all is black, then know that it is in the state of putrefaction. When it passes through the fire and the color becomes saffron-yellow, understand this as the organization, and the body is perforated. And when the color becomes red, understand, O Artist, that the body is with its soul. And then understand that you must give it fire as above, until the rise and birth of the body. Just as I have said concerning this K in the generation of the red, so I say of K in the generation and mastery of the white, according to its own mode as explained above. For then, by these signs and the doctrine of the masters of this art, the artist will be able to work securely.

# On the Tables and the Multiplication of the Art

Thus, the letters **b. t. v. x. y. z.** are arranged in a triple order. These points are divided as **m n o q**, which are certain ratios given to the letters **b. t. v. x. y. z.**, according to the names of the ancient principles. Some of these are divided and multiplied through the ratios of the parts **l. m. n. o. p. q.** and the aforementioned **n. p. r. q.** Because **l. m. n. o. p. m. q.** is made by multiplication from their multitude, one virtue <note>or "power/property"</note> is held from all of these and from their multiplication. This multiplication extends beyond unity, namely through **l.** from itself alone and not from another. By this virtue, each of the said **b. t. v. x. y. z.** would have certain qualities which they otherwise would not possess. I seek the truth expressed in the multiplication existing in the present time, such that the ratios fall so that an increase of their redness <note>original: "rubet"</note> occurs, and the work of our multiplication is finished.

The doctrine of the tables in the mastery of the work is now completed. # On the Generation of the Fire-Spirit

The fire-spirit <note>original: "phyralis"; likely referring to a vital or elemental heat</note> is not generated from angles, because the end of the collection of these things, according to many, would not be generated in the same way as it is in a tree. The fire-spirit is not generated unless it is brought forth according to that which was made near it. These things are demonstrated through the letters P, Q, Y, and V, which represent the two artists <note>The "artists" here likely refer to the active principles or the practitioners of the alchemical art</note> who must operate through different lines, touching the **red triangle** and naming each of these according to its own voice. Likewise, by moving the angle and the hour so that a distinction is made, that which is first in the two primary elements—the first light from which the mastery begins—is distinguished by those things which will be the sum of all primaries. This occurs through the middle according to the highest mode of different fathers, according to which many equal species of these artists can be named.

For in this way, those things which have arisen from the **red triangle** appear clearly in four rounded angles, at whose angles one can signify these reasons. From this triangle, the two artists can be well-observed. It is not given to men to have mastery over the red triangle; rather, the artist must deduce them through the **black triangle**, according to which each of these is greater in proportion than the other. For that which is greater is L, and L is Ph <note>likely abbreviations for philosophical or elemental terms</note>. This is seen through the truth of the middle, for they are correlated to one another. Because of this equality, it is necessary to lead them upward—namely E, G, A, H, B, F, G, and G, H, and H, I—so that also in the quantity of the substance, K might be generated qualitatively. For all men standing by this figure according to their own mode, there is another thing concerning the application of this triangle to the principle of this figure. We leave this to the well-instructed artist; the artist must also apply the different lines to the **black triangle**. Through this application, the artist will find the greatest secrets of the entire **physical mastery** <note>original: "phyci magist'y"; the study of nature and matter</note>, which has been labored for through its degrees. One principle follows another, placed in the practice of the mastery and above these things.

<margin>
And through that smallest thing, R, V, and J are measured and collected. It seeks its own suitable nature and does not respect the damage of misfortune. Because R and R are first changed, the mode of service is found in mixed names. It prepares the generative power, for that nature neither stands above the first things nor below them. For the two rotations and being from the middle, according to the mode of the point or the difference of the two, because it is in those things which are seen. By placing and affirming or denying the two principles, according to whether they are affirmable or deniable, the differences P, T, V, Y, and P are led, and they can be transferred and transmuted in the absence of E, F, G, H, J, and K. And through the position of the letters, a negative derivation is held because the local medium is lacking—which is K, S, R, Q, U, F, F, G, H, J. When these are lacking, the triangle stands on every side, through which the generation and corruption of the body B, T, V, X, Y, Z must occur. This happens through the difference of the greats and the difference of corruptions. Let B, R, V, P, Y, and Z be transmuted into I, L, and T, because it is possible that the difference of the two graduated things E, F, G, H, J, and K—in the mastery of these bodies—transfers the absence of B, T, V, X, Y, and Z to L.

And thus, through the difference of the two, it is possible to see F, F, G, U, F, J, naming B, T, V, P, Y, Z. According to the graduation of the two, E, F, G, and J, the artists who hold the affirmative position can, in case of necessity, increase the B, T, V, X, Y, Z. These are changed into F concerning death; it is necessary that the causes under their forms be altered, since they cannot be changed into F under their own forms unless they are transferred. This is what the circle and the science of the artists' affirmation and negation want. It can be regulated through the intellect in other affirmations and negations which are the principles of the whole induction of the principle of the art. That is, the difference must be able to be made by the spirit abstracted from B, T, V, X, Y, Z. It is answered that it will not, because the corporeal medium will be lacking. In the absence of P and Y, one cannot transmute B, T, V, P, and Z into their own species. This is the meaning of the "difference of the middle," which must be composed of the two B, T, V, Z and O, X, Y, U. These are a certain natural medium, grasping each of those things which, by reason of the gradation it has with the two B, T, V, and Z, gives them a place through all their species, so that in the smallest part of the two, its subtlety penetrates.

# On the Graduation of the Branches

In a twofold way, and concerning this, let the **artist** <note>Latin: *artista*; refers to the alchemical or technical practitioner.</note> receive the instruction to declare through a figure the form of forms and the form which the degrees of the branches have, for the sake of declaration. In this figure also, it is necessary for the artist to place three other angles so that he may regulate himself in each of the branches, so that he may be able to attain the proper ones.

## Copy of the Alphabet and its meanings from the testament of the great Raymond Lull <note>Ramon Llull (c. 1232–1315) was a philosopher and mystic to whom many later alchemical works were attributed.</note>
- **A.** Signifies God
- **B.** Signifies the wisdom of God
- **C.** Signifies vapors composed of water and earth and they are in their own power, etc.
- **D.** Signifies clear water deposited from the said vapors with the condensation of its nature, which is seen in those vapors by the excess made immediately of quicksilver, which [is] all small mobile air and windy places perforated under the earth and penetrates sulfurous minerals caused by hot and dry vapors.
- **E.** Signifies vitriol which is near to metallic matter, generated immediately from the matter of the aforesaid quicksilver and conceived from the said dry and sulfurous vapor in its resolution and motion by the compression of multiplication, the mineral heat of which [is...]
- **F.** Signifies vapors immediately generated which is the life of metals, [generated] from the said vitriol by sublimation and the ascent of the unial spirit, and this is the first and proximate matter of the generation of all metals conceived from natural heat quickened in form, etc.
- **G.** Signifies sulfur made immediately <gloss>through</gloss> living water generated from the aforesaid water, namely from the water of vapors, the congealing of all quicksilver which is the restraint of the divine vapor in the honey itself or vapor.
- **H.** Signifies metals generated from vapors or of sulfur and quicksilver and very little decoction, which are the extremes of the most upright.

# Accusatory Letter of Raymond Lull to Robert, King of France, concerning the Philosophers' Stone

->In the name of the holy Trinity and the infinite unity of the Creator, Amen.<-

**S**ince I, Raymond of the island of Majorca, have previously written various books and composed the art of transmutation, and have written the oldest of all books concerning the Philosophers' Stone <note>Latin: *lapis philosophorum*, the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold</note> according to its virtues—which I have learned from God and from distinct persons in every part, just as was transmitted to King Robert in the common tongue—I have known for certain and through labor that in this art there is a lying deception. Thus, anyone's operations, even those perceived through influence and a certain application of ingenious artifice, are seen to be varied errors. Therefore, I have composed all my books under such a name and style as I wished, so that as far as the writing is concerned, no root of error might occur. You may know this in the *Book of the Testament* and the *Apertorium* <note>The *Apertorium* (The Opener) was a famous alchemical treatise attributed to Lull</note> where I have treated all things most clearly, which happened to be done in part. I believe you have already read these books fully and understood them deeply. However, I admonish you regarding what you will find in them: that you should first study to please God, and keep your labors and all things revealed to you in the secret of your mind. Do not scatter this treasure among the unworthy <note>Latin: *idinos*, likely *indignos*</note>, lest I call down God's judgment upon this. To all those who have been delayed by God <gloss>f. quantity</gloss> if I can burden them with all things, because it is worthy of God. I found your letter by the hand of a messenger sent from you, which I read with diligent study. This mandate was compared by our people; however, I was able to extract certain books of medicine from the leaders in Salerno <note>Salerno was the site of the most important medieval medical school</note>, which you sent to me in a most grateful light where you intended

<column-break/>

that from the ingenuity of the art, the Stone might be seen if it could be given to you. The fear of God is preferred over my other books; or rather, that which is in all of ours is what is understood in the glosses, that I may begin to make other principles. All syllogisms, even those never before written, are in its power. Wherefore, if you understand my writings—and it is not less than the others—choose for yourself my application of principles.

**W**e hold that the [nature] of our Stones is more noble and more efficacious than I have declared in my other books, so that I may grant your petition.
<margin>The substance of the Grain</margin>
I speak the truth of minerals: the whole form is the matter of minerals, which is taken in two waters. One of these becomes a volatile stone without [heavy] labor. The other, however, is with fixed things <note>In alchemy, "fixed" substances resist the fire, while "volatile" ones evaporate</note>. I think that this water is gathered as our [menstruum] <note>A solvent, often called the "philosophical menstruum"</note> made in a cloth from things of which the water of the world is stronger and mortal, whose spirit flows through the whole world. It is provided lest it flee from you during the washing, which is labored at with ingenuity. Also, the Stone [is made] in a shorter time and with great strength of taste.

**T**he Animal Stone: A collection which has no end in itself; rule the elements in which there is less Earth than in any other stone, and there the greatest secrets of nature can be [extracted], not only regarding the generation of the stone, but also regarding the operations of transmutation. I shall declare this in the *Apertorium*. The effect of this stone is infinite.
<margin>Vegetable</margin>
**T**he Vegetable Stone: As far as it is long, and as if it were the animal stone regarding the [finishing] of the thing. Its effects transcend the animal [stone]. But the Great Elixir in the vegetable [stone] is such that it seems a miracle to the inventor.

He references his previous works, the Testament and Apertorium, as the definitive guides to these transmutations.</summary>

The full effect of transmutation and the truth of change is found through the **vegetable stone** <note>original: *lapide vegetabile*; likely referring to organic-based alchemical substances rather than minerals</note>, for its goodness and vast magnitude are discovered therein. It is said that through the **fifth essence** <note>original: *quinta esencia*; the "quintessence" or purest concentrated spirit of a substance</note> with which the stone itself is impregnated in the world, it acts either by itself or with a mineral spirit made from corrosives. From this incorruptible fifth essence, let the seeker know through arduous genius that the fifth essence has the power to mortify the spirits of mineral stones so they are less broken by poisons. This supreme medicine is sometimes used against certain ailments in human bodies, as if it were joined from blood.

In the vegetable realm, we shall find the most certain preservation of the human body from all accidental corruption. And thus, those who know and transmute are under the body of the fifth essence; if it is prepared for its proper end, their work will be famous, noble, and stable. You asked about the **shortening of the way** <note>original: *accurtatione*; a common alchemical request for a faster method to reach the "Great Work"</note>: there are two methods in all things—**cautery** <note>original: *cauterium*; here meaning a process of purification by fire or sharp alkaline salts</note> and the reduction from perfection, which, by means of the fifth essence, would possess every effect of transmutation.

The **cautery** of mineral stones is interpreted by itself; through it, you will find in them the fruit of transmutation. Let it not be diminished except by the first **calcination** <note>reduction to powder by heat</note> and by infusion over the first water, which must be very limpid and clear.

# On the Distillation of the Elixir

¶ Therefore, place in any **flask** <note>original: *boccia*, a round-bottomed glass vessel</note> one pound of **burning water** <note>original: *aqua ardens*, high-proof distilled alcohol</note> and one ounce of **ferment** <note>original: *fermenti*, likely gold for the red elixir or silver for the white</note> that has been well and optimally purified and beaten into leaves. You should have a furnace with its **cooling-chamber** <note>original: *gelo*</note> where the heat of the charcoal fire can be distributed through the arm of the furnace at a tempered heat. There, place your vessels and start the fire. And this is a most excellent fire, because this fire does not provide more heat than is necessary. For the **vials** <note>original: *apulle*</note>, as soon as they feel the heat, immediately dissolve the **refined material** <note>original: *finetum*</note>. Then, for a while, tie a sponge to the hollows of the **alchemical still** <note>original: *alchemis*</note>, which should be well-fitted to the head of the **still**, and very thick. Where the orbits are, there should be a service where you keep the sponges continually moistened with cold water. And with the continuous fire many times completed, you will see all the **refined material** ascend with its water; and once distilled, I set it aside in another vessel continually. And from this fiery apparatus, you will see that each pound distills twice in the day and twice in the night, and there remains continually one part in the vessel for as much as ascended in the other vessel... And in its own way you will see it ascending and descending... you will see how by reason of the heat the spirit is subtilized and thickened. And this is the **menstruum** <note>a solvent</note> of the arts. If you distill it continually, the water ascends in degrees of subtilization and sharpness, and you will see continually that the **refined material** is thickened; for the more this distillation is done with a gentle fire, the more subtle the spirit will be in strength and fire-power over the **refined material**.

It is necessary that this medicine be made from the best and highest quality, so that it may be completed through its proper methods. In ordinary waters, there are few spirits, and they act only upon the surfaces; other spirits remain fixed within them as coarse matter. Thus, the medicine would sometimes be fleeting and not intimately fixed within the core. If the spirits are only at the extremities, the medicine perishes immediately. <note>The author argues that the "spirits" or active volatile principles must penetrate the heart of the matter to be effective.</note> Therefore, proceed through solutions in a bath <note>likely a *balneum Mariae* or water bath</note>, as is the practice with vegetable substances.

It should be known that this Stone is not produced from mixed substances, but is vegetable in its own right; nevertheless, it is dissolved more easily than a mineral because of certain fixations used so that the medicine may penetrate more deeply. Then, the medicine is well-penetrating and fixed, which changes it for the better; and the more it penetrates, the more it nourishes the whole body and becomes more clear.

And so that I may write everything to you in the briefest possible way: you should know that through the "Lead of the Philosophers" <note>original: "plumbo philosophorum"; a code name for a starting material, often antimony or a specific lead ore</note> a certain oil of golden color is dissolved. This is used with the mineral stone or a mixture, and afterwards fixed. In the first sublimation <note>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then solidifies again</note>, it will work for you within four days, sparing you from all the labor of further purification and coagulation.

The reason is that this is the "Oil of All Things," which makes the medicine penetrable, agreeable, and desirable to all bodies; it increases their effect beyond measure, such as exists nowhere else in this world. From this, two wonders arise: that it was accessible to all the ancient philosophers, and that it separates the similar from the dissimilar. Those who labor in the manner of mixing for many days rarely find the Stone; but this oil is not the least among vegetable things, which through solutions and coagulations—as has been said—was in the Egg. <note>The "Philosophical Egg" refers both to the vessel used and the theory that the Stone contains the yolk (soul), white (spirit), and shell (body).</note> However, if it undergoes sublimation, where I believe the remedy of the Stone is much [...]

### The Softening of Any Hard Body
<margin>Note: very excellent</margin>
Take the marrow of any fat animal <note>original: "aialis pinguis"</note> and new wax in equal parts. Mix them together and distill over a slow fire through a <term>retort</term> <note>a glass vessel with a long neck used for distillation</note> of very clean sand. Collect the clear water: and in it, extinguish the molten hard body. If necessary, extinguish the glowing metal in it several times.

### The Softening of Glass and Affected Sinews
<margin>Try this</margin>
Take human or pig blood and cuttlefish bone <note>original: "sepies"</note>; distill through an alembic. With this water, rub the sinew strongly. Apply crushed glass; it will heal the limb with such a sinew, and it will soften the glass.

### To Know How to Remove Gold from a Cup Without Melting the Cup
<margin>Ounce</margin>
Take 1 <term>ounce</term> of borax and 3 <term>ounces</term> of spring water. Grind the borax very well. Then put it all into a pot and boil it for the space of one hour. Then, wetting the cup with that water, have powdered sulfur nearby and sprinkle it over the cup. Then place the cup over a charcoal fire until it is quite red. Then you shall wash it with <term>aqua fortis</term> <note>literally "strong water," usually nitric acid</note> and scrub it hard with a <term>scrubber</term> <note>original: "beryna"</note> made of pigskin. The gold will be drawn to the bottom of the aqua fortis; rinse it with spring water, etc.

### For Cementing Gold <note>A process of purifying gold using heat and salts</note>
Take crushed and sifted brick <note>original: "ragiola"</note> (two parts), common salt with oil, and crushed and ground copper (one part). Then take strong vinegar and wash the gold with fine glass. Then you shall take the pieces and throw them into the vinegar. And when you wish to <unclear>apply</unclear> the <term>cement</term>, take the pieces out of the vinegar and make a layer of the powder and another of the pieces. Give it fire little by little, <term>increasing it</term> until the furnace is white <unclear>with heat</unclear>. Then maintain a tempered fire and let it be for 36 hours.

# For hardening iron: so that other iron can be cut with it as if it were wood.

Take iron in the form of a sword or a blade, or fashioned into other shapes, and before it is tempered in water: let it be dipped six times in a mixture of equal parts of male pig fat <note>original: "assungia porci masculi"</note> and goose fat: and the more it is dipped, the better. Each time it should be brought to the fire, and the smith must take care that the iron does not touch water until, as said above, the iron has been dipped nine times in the said fats.

# Item for hardening iron.

To harden iron so that it cuts and marks. <term>Take earthworms</term>: which are found in the earth while the earth is being dug or plowed. Take an equal amount of radish and let them be well pounded. Their juice should be squeezed out through a cloth, each one separately by itself. Then mix together an amount of olive oil equal to a fourth part of those juices. Then extinguish the glowing hot iron in the said juices: and it will work wonderfully.

# Another experiment for iron for the same purpose.

Take the juice of willow root and the juice of radish in equal parts <note>original: "an[na]" for "ana," a medical term meaning 'of each'</note>. Temper the iron in the said juices and you will see wonders.

# For separating Silver from tin.

Take iron filings wrapped in Greek pitch <note>a type of pine resin</note> softened at the fire; mix the molten <term>silver</term> <note>original: "luna," the alchemical name for silver</note> with this iron: and the tin will adhere [to the iron] and the silver alone will remain.

# For catching birds

To catch birds with your hands: Take grain placed in dregs of wine and mixed with vinegar <note>original: "acuta," likely acetum</note>, and scatter it in small pieces in a place; if the birds eat from that place, they will not be able to fly.

# For favor and Love

Carrying the teeth of a wolf, or its skin, or the eyes of a wolf's foot <note>likely a reference to a specific part of the paw or a botanical "wolf's eye"</note> brings prosperous success, and procures and moves the friendship or favor of great men.

# For composing Lapis Lazuli [Blue Pigment]

Take one part <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note> and two parts of green copper <note>verdigris</note>. Grind them very well, put them together and moisten them into the form of a paste with oil of tartar. Place it in a glass flask well-luted <note>sealed with clay</note> and well-closed. Place it in the steam of bread after the bread has been removed, for 6 days: and you will find it then to be an excellent preparation.

# How azure is made from lead

Take lead and beat it into thin sheets and place it in a pot well-sealed with grape husks in wine for 14 days. Open it and you will find the "Greek flower" <note>a chemical crust</note>... because it is <term>azure</term> <note>blue pigment</note>. Return the same sheets into the wine dregs until they are all converted into azure.

# For writing golden letters with a quill

Take <term>gum arabic</term> and dissolve it well in water. Let it be moved by the gum: and with this, grind the material until it remains thick like a small loaf. To this, afterwards add some prepared gold... and grind it very well and then strongly. Then put in some water... and lift the hand with the finger... and without pausing the water... so that nothing adheres to it... afterwards throw out the water until you see the <term>gold</term> move. And a third time put in new water: and do this three or four times, until the water is clear and separated from the gold and the dross material that was in the mortar. And when you wish to work, take a little of the said material and dissolve or temper it in gum water: and write what you wish!

### To make letters of gold
Take some fine crystal: and grind it well, and then take some water of gum arabic <note>A natural gum made of hardened sap from acacia trees, used as a binder.</note>: and some egg white: and dissolve this crystal with that gum water and with this egg white: until it flows from the pen: as the master does: and then write whatever you wish. And then let it dry: and then take gold leaf and strike it <note>Apply or press it</note> upon this letter: you will have letters of gold.

### If you wish to have letters of silver
Take some silver: and strike it upon these letters: you will have letters of silver; this is proven.

### To lay down gold
<note>Original: "Ad ponendum aurum"</note>
Take well-ground gypsum <note>A soft sulfate mineral used as a base for gilding</note>: and a third part of tartar glue <note>A binder made from cream of tartar or wine dregs</note>: and add a measure of flour <note>Original: "flore larthe," likely fine wheat flour</note>: and place it on the paper where you wish to put the gold: and allow it to dry well. This being done, first scrape it well with a knife: then put clear water upon the said gypsum: very finely with a brush: and immediately apply the gold: and allow it to dry well. When this is dry: polish it with an amethyst stone: or with the tooth of a wolf or a dog or a bear: and thus you will see the gold at its best.

### To make flesh color
Take white lead <note>Original: "cerusa," a toxic lead pigment</note>: with a very little bit of well-ground cinnabar <note>A bright red mineral pigment (mercury sulfide)</note>.

### To remove letters
Take powder of white bone: and gypsum, 2 ounces. And grind it finely: and dissolve it with an egg yolk. And smear it over the letters: and then let it dry: and when it is dry: scrape it gently with a pen-knife: and the paper will remain clean.

## To make the paste.

First take six ounces of pine resin, half an ounce of whole mastic <note>a high-quality resin from the mastic tree</note>, half an ounce of new wax cut thin: and then take a small glazed earthenware jar and put it over the coals near the fire: and first put the resin inside: and let it melt well, constantly stirring with a wooden spatula: and then put in the mastic and let it melt well with the other things. And when the aforesaid things are well melted and dissolved: have ready a barrel half-full of clean water and have a cloth over this barrel: and strain the aforesaid things down into the water through this cloth, and squeeze it well out of the said cloth. And when you have squeezed it well, take that strained mixture which is in the said barrel in your hands: and make a paste of it in the manner of a loaf of bread: always working it by hand: and often grease your hands with linseed oil: and work this paste by hand so much that it becomes supple like wax.

<column-break/>

and so that it stretches flexibly while well warm. And this being done, take the powder of lapis lazuli <note>a precious blue semi-precious stone</note> and you must incorporate it well into this paste little by little, always working the said paste by hand: and still greasing your hands occasionally with the said oil. And when you have incorporated it well: put this paste in a glazed stone bowl: and grease the bowl with the said oil: and let the said paste stay in the said bowl for eight days. And when you wish to extract the said blue <note>ultramarine pigment</note> out of the said paste: take a glazed stone platter that is a little shallow and not deep, and have two small sticks that are a span long and as thick as twice the thumb of the hand. And put a little sweet lye <note>original: "liçima/lixia"; an alkaline solution made from wood ashes</note> that is warm into the said platter where the paste is; if it is winter time, use the lye, but if it is summer time, do it with fresh water that is clear and beautiful. And when you draw out a little of the blue: pour it into a glazed earthenware bowl: and do this for six or eight bowls, adding the water or the said lye little by little: until you have taken it all out of the said paste: and so pour it from one bowl into another, taking the finest: until you reduce it into three grades <note>original: "carue"; likely meaning qualities or sorts</note>, that is, in three manners: and of three values. One shall be the finest: the other less fine: and the other even less fine: and thus you will have your blue complete.

## To wash azure or to revive it.
Always do this with clear, slightly warm water, and then with cold water. And always take care that you do not wash it with a warm hand, or with strong water <note>original: "acqua forte," likely referring to an acidic solution or nitric acid</note>. And you must add a little white honey to it.

## To make German azure.
Take the yolk of an egg and grind the azure well with the egg yolk. When it is ground very fine to your liking, wash it well with lye <note>original: "lissia," a strong alkaline solution used for cleaning</note> until the redness is gone. Then use it for whatever you wish. And try it, for this is proven.

## How German azure is washed.
Take the foam that comes from white cloth when they are boiled in the cauldron; wash the said azure with this foam and you will have as beautiful a color as you could desire.

## A good tempera for ultramarine azure to write with a pen.
First take the azure and grind it upon a serpentine stone <note>a type of green-mottled stone used for grinding pigments</note> with gum water. Then take a drop of egg yolk and put it in your <unclear>vessel</unclear>, and it will be ready for writing with a pen.

## To highlight azure with saffron.
Take a little saffron and a little white lead <note>original: "biaccha," a lead-based white pigment</note> and mix them together. With that color, you can then highlight the azure placed on paper. And that is how it is done.

## To temper azure when you wish to work with a pen.
Take some gum arabic water and temper the azure with it. And when

<column-break/>

preparing the said water, wash the said gum with a little lukewarm water. When it is clear, take some similarly lukewarm water and put it into the said gum. Ensure that it has the consistency of honey to the touch; let it be tempered thus.

## How cinnabar is made.
Take quicksilver <note>mercury</note> and well-ground sulfur. Place them in a glass flask in such a way that the sixth part is sulfur and the seventh is quicksilver <note>The author likely means a ratio of 6 to 7 or specific parts of the whole</note>. Then take earth and horse dung and mix them together. Coat the flask with this paste so that nothing of the flask is visible except the opening through which it can breathe. Place it in the furnace until the smoke coming out of the vent appears red. Then take it from the fire and let it cool, and it will be good cinnabar.

## When you wish to write with gold.
Take a quantity of fine beaten gold and take some honey and grind them together on the porphyry stone, just as one makes color. Then take a little hot water and mix it together; the gold will all go to the bottom. When you wish to use it, temper that gold with egg white and with gum. Then work with it, and it is good for writing.

## To make purpurina.
Take sal ammoniac <note>ammonium chloride</note>, tin, quicksilver, and sulfur: two ounces of each. Proceed as you did for the cinnabar.

## To make good brazilwood.
Take some brazilwood <note>original: "verzino," a red dye derived from wood</note> and grate it, or cut it small, or scrape it with glass. Then put it in a small pot

### To draw oil out of paper

### For the same

### When the paper has become wrinkled

### To remove a spot of grease from paper
Place a wet white cloth over the paper. and then put on some crushed powdered gypsum. and then a white cloth and then gypsum. and squeeze the book.

To extract azure <note>original: "azurum"; likely ultramarine blue from lapis lazuli</note>: take a glazed vessel and put in it lukewarm water; work the paste through your hands, and the water will be drawn out like a serene sky. ### For etching iron
Take 3 ounces of saltpeter <note>original: "Salis nitri"</note>, 4 ounces of common salt, 4 ounces of white tartar, 4 ounces of rock alum <note>original: "Alumino rotte"</note>, 3 ounces of verdigris <note>original: "Viridis enis"</note>, 3 ounces of orpiment <note>original: "auripigmenti"; an arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, 2 ounces of sal ammoniac, and a quantity of Roman vitriol. Keep them in a very clean mortar, so that no oiliness is mixed in. Let the said powders be sifted and placed in a glazed jar, and do this three times; with eight pounds of fresh water. And while it is cooked, let the whole be stirred together with a clean stick until a third part of the water is consumed. Then let it be stored in a glass vessel and stopped up very wisely so that it does not breathe. And with the said water, smear the warmed iron, which has been well polished.

### Strong glue that does not fear water
Take stag's horn, and a little bit of old <unclear>tōigule</unclear>, and naval pitch, and iron filings in equal parts; and grind them together; and prepare it with egg white and a little bit of honey over the fire. Smear what you wish, and it will not fear water.

### To soften crystal and give it whatever color you want
Take the blood of an old he-goat fed for 14 days on ivy leaves, and 5 pounds of goose blood, and 2 ounces of oil dregs <note>original: "morcha d’oglio"; the sediment from olive oil pressing</note>, 1 ounce of strong vinegar, 5 ounces of rock salt, 2 ounces of rock alum, and 1 ounce of <term>scagliola alum</term> <note>a type of alum used in plasterwork or dyeing</note>. Boil all these things together, and put inside the crystal that you wish to soften, and let it stay for 7 days; and then you can give it the color that pleases you. And when you wish to take it out from that place where it has been tinted and softened, you shall put it in cold water and it will become hard as it was at first; and you may polish it according to your entire will.

### To tint crystal with color
The mixture for crystal is made red: make a <term>lye</term> <note>original: "capitello"; a strong alkaline solution</note> of ashes from vine branches, and of ashes <margin>from the spindle tree</margin> from the spindle tree <note>original: "gerzo"; likely the Euonymus europaeus</note>, and of quicklime. Let it boil over the fire until it is reduced to a third; and with that third part, dissolve the color that you wish to give to the crystal, and pour the liquid over the top.

### To dissolve Crystal
Crystal is dissolved if it is placed in water resolved from tartar, lime, salt, and rock alum. And this same water deletes spots from the face and renders it wonderfully beautiful.

# On the composition of the stone of the
## philosophers, an elegant doctrine
## composed in the one hundred verses
## written below.

My son, I now offer you a good doctrine.
<note>original: "Sumuz thesauzu tene meri dat forisau" - This line contains corrupted Latin/vernacular mix, likely meaning "Hold the greatest treasure which the pure [source] gives forth."</note>
Embrace this, beloved, lest it be taken from you.
Dissolve the chains and revolve the sayings of the wise.
In the beginning of Alchemy, you shall stand and learn the pillars,
And which authors you shall take, and you shall receive the honors of kings.
This art deceives fools, but through many problems
It releases the minds of the wise by the virtue of God.
This art is desired by many; here the truth is given
To those whom God accepts when He scepters them with such a gift.
This art is dear, brief, and light, and also rare,
And these hundred verses give the completion to them.
The Art requires one single thing which anyone knows well;
Many things adapt this, yet the thing is in one.
Nothing is similar to it, and the thing is also cheap in price.
Nor should it be despised, for it performs stupendous things.
You must fix this and tame it in the fire,
So that the vapors may ascend and return again to the depths.
Dissipate the captured thing, then [it is] prepared without filth.
Gently extracted, thus crush and break the mass.
The harsh thing becomes smooth in pleasant vessels.
<margin>Gomphus <note>A bolt or nail; here likely referring to a binding agent or a specific stage of "fixing" the substance.</note></margin> Which, while it is calcined <note>reduced to powder by heat</note>, is loved by the learned.
But while this thing is fixed and remains in the fire,
A shadow covers it, [yet it is] the fifth substance <term>Quintessence: the purest, fifth element beyond earth, air, fire, and water</term>.
It joins all things; if it melts, it melts all things.
And since it is fixed, it does not receive anything unless it is fixed.
This thing adapts itself if, having been turned, it is moistened.
This thing dries if it is roasted with [other] things.
Sing like the mountains, the regions, and the fountains.
This thing is in action while it becomes a powder without touch.
Simple, corroded, it will be subtle and precious.
If it scorns the fire, it does not turn toward sublime things.
Entering then the waters, for they render the bodies <unclear>liquid</unclear>.
It makes those who possess it reign and makes the buried live again.
The form of the world is the most correct rule for this art,
Nor should nature attempt what is committed to it

<column-break/>

Except that which is finished not in haste, but in the order of time.
The water of Juno <note>likely a poetic term for a specific solvent or "mercurial" water</note> joins the earth and the fire.
In a fragile mixture, the fifth thing <insert>the quintessence</insert> comes upon it,
Which commands the mixture to enter and to vary.
The ferment <term>Ferment: a substance, like yeast, added to "leaven" the base metal into gold</term> must [act] through similar species.
No offspring ever arises without seed.
The seeds are right, but the ferment of the species
Brings a single substance to the nascent thing and begets
One from the other, if corruption occurs within it.
In which, while it dies, it is said to give fertile seed.
Thus the food in the stomach receives a wondrous ferment,
Which is pure, and likewise passes through the limbs.
And the human seed, born from pure blood,
Extracted from the kidneys, is taken up by the cell of the womb.
Joined with the female seed, it becomes as one.
Then the innate heat first [forms] the parts of this;
It forms the extremities, then the skin, then discerns the limbs.
It feeds him here until the time of exit is present.
And the ferment of the thing is the thing itself, but stayed by the spirit <note>original: "pneumate"</note>;
It wishes for its own, without which nothing ferments from it.
The spirit of the ferment joined with the spirit of the mixture
The skin encloses, so that its brief [power] may be in them.
Art perishes in place of the skin while nature follows the vessel.
The metallic work is through the seed which it takes within.
He who wished for the result resolved the joined phlegms.
The fixed thing restrains the bodies which it shapes by flux.
For that which remains without rest lasts the least.
If you defend the earth, then you catch everything volatile.
That is dried, this is dissolved, and this is tamed.
These are the things it shapes: that which it spreads and that which it tinges.
Art or nature draws the water out from the things.
These are the secrets in which one shall rejoice without end.
Four are made from one, and the four become one.
While they are corrupted together, this art receives one,
Which, well-purged, it places in the belly of the form.
To this, nature gives a double and multiplies it,
As the work is sublimated, captured, and dissolved in water.
Look to what kind it is, how much at first and how much after.

# On the Lute of Wisdom and how it should be made
Take tenacious earth <note>likely a heavy potter's clay</note> and let it dry thoroughly. Pulverize it until it is a fine powder. Mix it with water containing egg whites and pulverized horse dung. Once mixed and tempered, let it be smeared upon your vessel. When the first coat has dried, apply a second coat. <note>The "Lute of Wisdom" or *lutum sapientiae* was a specialized alchemical cement used to seal glass vessels so they could withstand high heat without cracking or leaking vapors.</note>

# How Azmonian Salt is made
Take one pound of human blood, two pounds of common salt, and six pounds of common water. Let all these be mixed and dissolved. Afterwards, distill the mixture through a filter. Then place it over a fire and leave it there until the moisture of the water evaporates. The "Azmonian salt" <note>original: *sal azmoniani*; likely a variant of *sal ammoniac* or a specific ritual salt</note> will remain.

<margin>Note: The method of Saint Viridarius</margin>
# Method for the composition of Verdigris
Take copper plates four fingers wide. Smear them with a composition made of strong vinegar, quicklime, and salt ammoniac. Take an earthen vessel in which you will place the said plates; let this vessel stand in a place where the sun's rays may touch it. Nevertheless, bury the vessel in warm horse manure. Pour into the same vessel strong vinegar made from red wine, along with the grape dregs <note>original: *fimis*, here referring to the pressed skins and stems</note> from which the wine was squeezed, or barley straw, or branches of vine-shoots, in such quantity that they rise above the vinegar by two or three fingers. Suspend the said plates in the vessel so that they do not touch the vinegar. Alternatively, place them upon the aforementioned grape dregs or straw, and then cover the plates with more dregs or straw, provided the plate has been smeared with the aforementioned liquid or composition. Continue this process, placing the smeared plates upon the dregs or straw until the vessel is full. Then cover and seal the vessel very well, and let it stand

<column-break/>

thus for 24 hours. Afterwards, having opened the vessel and extracted the plates, scrape off and collect the green substance <note>verdigris, or copper acetate</note> into a glazed earthen vessel. Continue this until you have a good quantity of the said verdigris. This quantity of verdigris you shall reduce to the form of an ointment using vinegar and urine. Place it in a bag made of ram's skin, compressing and filling it well. Having placed a weight on top, set it in the sun to dry, turning the bag continually in the sun so that it dries perfectly on all sides. And when it has been dried in the sun, you will have your perfect verdigris. <note>Verdigris was highly valued both as a pigment for illumination and for its medicinal properties in treating wounds.</note>

# Burnt copper is made thus: On burnt copper
Take calcined orpiment and grind it very finely; take very fine copper filings. Place them in a crucible over a gentle fire: a layer of the powdered orpiment, then another layer of filings. ### On increasing the weight of gold

<margin>A</margin>
And if the weight of the gold is lacking, it is given thus: dissolve alum <note>original: "alumen"</note> from the white in a crucible <note>original: "reuabulo"</note> over the fire. Once dissolved, take an equal amount 

<column-break/>

of good <gloss>correct</gloss> new earth <note>likely a specific type of clay or mineral earth</note>, which you shall dissolve little by little with the said alum in the crucible over the fire. Afterward, mix in the best clear vinegar. Then let it soak together, and skim the froth from the top of the crucible. By drawing out the froth, there will remain inside the side of the crucible a sort of fatness. When it is dissolved and well-mixed and completed, remove the fire from under the crucible and allow it to dry. 

When this is done, you will receive upon the vinegar a certain body like an ointment, hard like pitch. Of this, add double the amount of the gold that was made, which weighs less than other named gold. By putting your gold back into the crucible where it was dissolved, it will have the correct weight upon the fire.

### Concerning Red Saffron <note>likely referring to Crocus Martis, or red iron oxide</note>
If you wish to make a very red saffron: grind it very finely and incorporate it with an equal amount of sal ammoniac <note>ammonium chloride</note>. And place it to be sublimated over a slow fire, and the salt will sublimate in a red color. And the <term>residue</term> <note>original: "recm" (recrementum), the dross or leftover material</note> of iron or the burnt iron will remain at the bottom, very red. And some add cinnabar <note>mercury sulfide</note>, but I say that it is not necessary.

### A Work for Reddening and Giving the Color of Gold using <gloss>bull's gall</gloss>: but it does not withstand the cement <note>a refining process</note> but only has the color of florins

<margin>M M</margin>
Take 1 part of salt made from vitriol <note>iron or copper sulfate</note>, and an equal amount of sal ammoniac, and an equal amount of verdigris <note>green copper acetate</note>, and 2 parts of <margin>grain</margin> grain alum <note>likely a specific granular form of alum</note> made red. And temper it with strong red vinegar so <margin>silver</margin> that it is like a cement. Take some gold and make plates, and cement them with the said concoction. And let it stand thus for a whole day, reddening over burning coals. Afterward, let it cool, and you will find the plates well-colored inside and out. Afterward, cement them as before in the same concoction, and melt them in the cement; extinguish the whole melt in bull's gall

<column-break/>

in which gall there shall be dissolved 2 parts of the aforementioned alum and one part of vitriol, and let there be twice as much gall. And thus you will have good and fine gold in the color of <term>Florins</term> <note>the gold coins of Florence, famous for their purity and bright color</note>. And it is good for gilding and withstands melting, but it does not withstand the cement <note>meaning the color is a surface or alloy enhancement that would be removed by rigorous chemical refining</note>. If you <unclear>wish</unclear> to quench it in the water of gold vitriols, it will be well; or in bull's gall as you wish. And in this work thus done, 2 carats are worth 3.

### Salt of Vitriol / Concerning the salt of vitriol
The aforementioned is made thus: Take vitriol and dissolve it in <term>said</term> <note>original: "dci" (dicti)</note> water, and let it settle. And distill it through a filter; afterward congeal it by fire, and thus you will have salt of vitriol. And that salt is very penetrating and gives a great red tint.

### For reddening grain alum
Likewise, the aforementioned grain alum is a little green. Dissolve it in strong white vinegar and distill it through an alembic <note>a distilling apparatus</note>. And all kinds of alums ought to be dissolved in vinegar and afterward congealed by fire. And thus dissolve it three times and congeal it as many times. [symbol] Furthermore, place that salt in a double glass vessel, and place that glass upon a furnace over ashes which are well-compressed under the glass and around the rim of the glass to the thickness of two fingers. [symbol] Furthermore, give it fire for one hour, and afterward make a fire for half a day and no more. Afterward, let it cool, and you will find the alum very red like scarlet. And you have alum properly prepared to be put into this work.

### On the preparation of sal ammoniac
You shall prepare sal ammoniac <note>ammonium chloride</note> thus: sublimated once. ### Precious powder for whitening
<note>original: "Pulvis preciosus ad album"</note>
Take one ounce of egg yolk, one ounce of marcasite <note>a iron sulfide mineral with a metallic luster</note>, one ounce of rock salt <note>original: "salis gemmae"</note>, one ounce of Jupiter <note>alchemical code for Tin</note>, and two ounces of orpiment <note>a deep yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>. Let all be pulverized and mixed with strong vinegar and cooked to the thickness of honey. Then let them dry. Next, make from this round pieces in the manner of hazelnuts and place them in the sun until they are well dried. Then grease them well and let them be ground, and add one drachm of pulverized antimony <note>original: "attemici"</note> and let the whole be mixed in vinegar. Add two drachms of pulverized tartar <note>potassium bitartrate, a common alchemical flux</note>, then dry the whole; and keep this precious preparation very well.

### How Moon can be made from Jupiter and Saturn
<margin>A H</margin>
A work for whitening. A certain person <unclear>again</unclear> made Moon <note>Silver</note> at Toledo. # For making silver from copper

# A Work for Silver, and for Removing
# the Shriek from Tin.

Take 2 parts of Jupiter <note>Tin</note>, which you shall melt well in an iron <unclear>crucible</unclear>. Put it, while still clean, into a glass vessel shaped like a musical instrument <note>likely a lute-shaped flask</note>. Keep this vessel, which has been sealed with the "mud of wisdom" <term>luto sapientie: a clay sealant used to airtight alchemical vessels</term>, over a fire for a long time while it makes a noise, until the shriek is removed from the tin. You shall, however, place a good distilling <term>alembicū: a distilling apparatus</term> over the vessel, using 3.5 ounces of a very strong kindling mixed with crushed salt. After an hour, when the spirit <note>the vapor</note> wishes to ascend, you shall remove it from the fire. Once it is extracted from the vessel in this molten state, place it in very strong vinegar, repeating the process three times in a salt solution. Then take the cubed grinding stones which have been moistened a little with water, and hammer it diligently in a pit in the earth until they harden together. Afterwards, you shall make a pit there of the same size as the quantity of tin appears to be. Then take a third part of <term>azurini: likely a blue mineral or pigment like lapis lazuli or azurite</term>, which has been heated until it glows, in its own thread

<column-break/>

of calf-skin and "beard of Jupiter" <note>a common name for the plant Sempervivum tectorum, used here as an organic additive</note> thrown in. Grind it, but mix in a third part of the tin, so that after they have been ground together, the tin clearly disappears. Pour the medicated molten metal through a thick filter into the aforementioned pit. Then, take the blue mineral heated to the point of glowing and place it upon the filtered bar, so that a sudden glowing does not occur. Once mixed, melt it again and soak it in very strong vinegar in a salt solution. Wash it in that same vinegar until the vinegar no longer turns black. Afterwards, wash those lucky pieces in clear water until the water remains clear. Finally, gather those lucky pieces together and melt them again, and you will have Moon <note>Silver</note> that withstands all tests.

# A Work for the Red—that is, which
# converts into the red color of Gold.

Take 1 part of Venus <note>Copper</note>, which you shall wash with diligence using a file, vinegar, and salt for a long time until no greenness <note>verdigris</note> appears in the vinegar. Then wash it in clear water until it is certain the water remains clean. Afterwards, take two crucibles <term>cruciulos: small melting pots</term> and place in the bottom of them a bed of the aforementioned filings, first dried in the sun. Then place a bed of the stalks of small beans, cut up; then another bed of the aforementioned filings; then another bed of <term>calamine: a zinc ore used to turn copper into brass, which looks like gold</term>; then another of filings; then another of <term>patmina: likely a mineral earth or pigment</term>; then reddish blue mineral; then another layer of bean stalk fragments, until the crucible is full.

### Work for the Red from Venus
<note>Venus refers to Copper</note>

<margin>Copper (🜔)</margin>

Take strong vinegar and soak [the metal] in oil for one day; afterward in vinegar of salted tartar, or with alum if you wish, or simply in vinegar for one day. Wash it in water, and it will be beautiful. 
Take a cauldron and fill it with ash; place in it the vessel called an alembic <note>a distilling apparatus</note>, in which you place the vinegar prepared as just described, without mixing any other thing. ## To compose the water which is called the purifying water, fixing and stabilizing all spirits
<note>original: "aqua mundi fixans et fixans omnes spiritus"</note>

## Concerning the water that pertains to this art

Take <note>The symbol ℞ stands for "Recipe," the standard opening for medical and alchemical formulas.</note> tallow or fat of a goat, half a pound, and a quantity of strong vinegar <note>original: "vmagre"</note>, and an equal amount of rainwater. Add salt of tartar <note>Potassium carbonate</note> and 1 ounce of mercury <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note> of the scrapings. From the aforementioned mixtures, add 4 drams of the "precious and moistening" mixture of radish and 3 drams of sulfur <note>represented by the symbol 🜍</note>. Mix all these things and place them in a glass alembic <note>A chemical still used for distillation</note>. Seal it with "wisdom lute" <note>A specialized airtight clay or paste used to seal alchemical vessels</note> and let it stand in the sun for 11 days, or over a slow fire. Afterward, have a furnace prepared for this work, similar to the furnace in which <gloss>one takes out</gloss> the bird <note>Likely a reference to the "Pelican" vessel or a specific heat-regulating furnace</note>. Let it be placed over the fire, and let a low fire of willow wood be made so that the water is distilled; then receive it. Afterward, take this noble water, which is worth more than gold <note>symbol: ☉</note> and more profitable than silver <note>symbol: ☾</note>. It is called "purifying water" <note>original: "aygua mundificans"</note>, for it fixes the spirits. Afterward, take the dregs <note>original: "fexa"</note> and let them be dried in the sun for 3 days. Keep them from water and humidity, and keep them well until they are needed.

## Precious water that pertains to this art

Take 3 ounces of water... 2 ounces of water... and 2 ounces of common salt <note>symbol: 🜔</note>. It is called "precious water." Keep this water. After this, take a quantity of gold <note>☉</note> filings and let them be treated with vinegar for

3 days. Afterward, let it be placed with other vinegar and let it be macerated for 3 days. Do this until it is all black. And if it is not black enough, return to the first step and keep it.

### On making oil of tartar which congeals and fixes spirits

A secret regarding oil of tartar: the method of preparation is: take the whitened [tartar] and let it be clear and burning.
<margin>Note here the oil</margin>
Dissolve the Mercury <note>$\unicode{x263F}$</note> in cold water and once the dissolution is made, let it be distilled through a filter; you will receive a clear white water. Place this in a cauldron that is not tinned, or in a vessel that is not glazed—or rather, one very diligently glazed—and it will congeal. And when it comes to the tested thickness so that it acts like a salt, then throw in a little cold water by hand and let it boil so that it returns to its first state of congealing. Then again add cold water as before; and let this be repeated so many times that it cannot be congealed by any fire. This will happen in 10 or 11 times, according to the strength of the primary tartar or the fire.

## On dyeing with a red color

<margin>Salt...</margin>
Take <note>The symbol 'Rx' stands for 'Recipe', the traditional opening for medical and chemical formulas.</note> six pounds of very strong vinegar that has stood in smoke or in the sun. Take another three ounces of madder <note>original: "rorthe", likely referring to the red dye plant Rubia tinctorum</note> and distill it through an alembic <note>term: alembic (a chemical apparatus used for distilling liquids)</note>. Take only that which is sublimated white; but if it is not changed, place it with the "father" <note>likely a reference to the base material or a primary vessel</note> and in the same place put three pounds of powdered white lead <note>term: ceruse (white lead, a common pigment in antiquity)</note>. Use the distilled vinegar until the white lead is dissolved. Place it under manure <note>fimum: decomposing manure was used as a steady, low-temperature heat source in early chemistry</note> for fifteen days. Remove it from the manure and you will find the white lead dissolved in the vinegar. Soak cinnabar <note>original: "singuber", a bright red mineral pigment</note> in this, then dry it in the sun. If you moisten it again, add more than 24 pounds of white lead.

## To make camphor

Take two pounds of vinegar distilled through an alembic and one pound of select and pure mastic <note>term: mastic (a resin gathered from the mastic tree, used in varnishes)</note>. If you do not have mastic, take in its place one pound of white vermilion <note>original: "vermins albe", likely a purified or synthetic mineral</note>. Powder it and place it in the vinegar; put it under manure for fifteen days. Extract it and place it in another glass vessel having a long neck so that the sun may act upon it thoroughly.

## To prepare camphor in the form of a loaf

Take two pounds of vinegar distilled through an alembic and one pound of select and mixed mastic. If you do not have mastic, take in its place one pound of clear white vermilion. Powder it and place it in the vinegar under manure for fifteen days. Extract it and place it in another glass vessel having a long neck, so that the sun may act upon it well within. Leave it

<column-break/>

in the sun for one day, and you will find the camphor congealed in the form of a loaf.

<margin>that is, prayer beads</margin>
## To make signs or prayer beads <note>original: "pater noster", referring to the beads of a rosary</note> out of amber

Take egg whites in which there is nothing of the egg yolks; beat them well into a foam and put them into a pig's gut that has been previously washed and dried. Do it in this way: blow up the washed gut with your mouth or a small reed, tie it with a thread, and dry the gut itself. Fill it with the egg white and <unclear>hōa</unclear>; place it in smoke for three weeks. The longer it stays, the redder it becomes. At the end of fifteen days, take it in your hand and you will find it hardened. Shape it into the form of prayer beads, large or small, as you desire. Pierce them with a gold wire and put them back into another gut to dry in an oven. The longer they stay in the oven, the more they are colored. When they have been dried, they ought to be polished on a stone slab <note>original: "tabulam murū", likely a marble or grinding slab</note> using powdered charcoal and linseed oil.

## To make sublimated white lead

Take one pound of white lead or silver litharge <note>term: litargiri (lead monoxide, a byproduct of silver refining)</note> and sublimate it in a single, well-luted <note>note: "luting" involves sealing a vessel with clay or paste to make it airtight</note> glass vessel over a very strong fire for three days and nights, blowing with bellows. You will find sublimated Alexandrian white lead.

## To make a powder for silvering any copper vessel.
<margin>B</margin>
Take sal ammoniac <note>ammonium chloride, used as a flux</note> and saltpeter <note>potassium nitrate</note> in equal weight, and a fourth part or a half part of silver—not the filings, but very fine silver—and mix them well together. Make a crucible red-hot in the fire and put all the said powders inside. Stir with a small wooden stick or an iron point until the moisture has evaporated, and it is done. When the copper vessel is clean and well-washed with water or the juice of citrons <note>original: "atranguli"; likely citrus medica, used for its acidity to clean metal</note>, by rubbing it with the said powder, it will be silvered and white.

## To alloy and color copper with gold by imitation; it will be good gold in color and weight of twenty carats.
<margin>¶</margin>
Take one dram <note>original: "ʒ . 1 ."</note> of alum of Zortha <note>a type of alum, possibly from a specific geographic region like Syria</note>, a quarter-part of rock salt, a quarter-part of common salt, half an ounce of <term>gramemo alum</term> <note>likely a corruption of "alume di piuma" or feathered alum</note>, two ounces of Roman vitriol <note>iron or copper sulfate</note>, one ounce of verdigris, and one ounce of tartar from a barrel <note>potassium bitartrate deposits from wine casks</note>. Take all these materials and pulverize them well. Take a glass carafe with the capacity of a <term>dobla</term> <note>a Spanish gold coin, here used as a measure of volume</note> and put all these materials inside; fill it with common water and boil it until half remains. Then take filings of brass or Cyprian copper <note>high-quality copper from Cyprus</note> and moisten them with this water. Then take raw mercury passed through goatskin <note>a method of purifying mercury by squeezing it through leather</note> and amalgamate the said copper filings with the mercury. Once amalgamated, place it in a crucible in the fire, moving it

<column-break/>

continually with a stick until it melts. Once melted, throw in as much weight of gold as there was of the Cyprian copper. It will be of excellent color and a weight of twenty carats, and you will be able to make any work of gold from it.

## For whitening red gold.
Take 2 ounces of red copper, beaten thin and cut small, 1 dram of white arsenic, 1 dram of tartar, and 1 dram of prepared salt. Grind them all together and place a layer of powder and a layer of the said copper inside a crucible; let the first and last layers be of powder. Seal the said crucible with a tile and good clay <note>a technique called "luting" to make the vessel airtight</note>, and bury it among the lit coals. Let it sit for one hour, then remove it. Add half an ounce of saltpeter and half an ounce of tartar, seal it as you did before, and pour it into molds <note>original: "cannali"</note>; it is done and most perfect.

It will come out red or black; to whiten it, take two parts of crushed tartar and one of common salt. Put them with water into a clean copper barrel and make it boil. When it boils, throw in...

### To give weight to "grossi" coins that do not have sufficient weight

### On the mutation of Tin and Mercury into the best Silver

Take, therefore, the Elidrium and an equal amount of **Silver**, and melt them together; and the whole [will be silver].

### On the Purification of Silver

Silver is purified and prepared in this way: first, let it be purified with lead. Afterward, once melted, let it be cast into small rods. These should be heated until glowing and quenched in vinegar <note>original: "deacet," likely a contraction for "de aceto"</note>. Each time they are heated until they are red, extinguish them in pig's blood. After the tenth time, beat it into thin plates and melt it with a little borax <term>Borax: a flux used in soldering and smelting to clean the metal surface</term> into new plates. Once melted, cast them again into small rods, and as before, extinguish them in vinegar while glowing. Melt them a third time, again beaten into plates with borax. And know for certain that you will have the softest and most purified silver. When this is melted, add to it a tenth part by weight of sulfur prepared for the "white work" <note>The "white work" or albedo is the stage in alchemy where the material is purified to a silver state</note>, and you will have silver of wonderful sound; and the aforementioned tin or lead will be melted quickly.

### The composition of the medicine, of which one part converts four parts of prepared moon into true sun

In the name of the Lord, let the prepared spirits be taken, namely: Orpiment <note>original: "Auripigmentum"; a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, sulfur, quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury</note>, and sal ammoniac. With the prepared things <note>likely "y" refers to a specific chemical shorthand or "hyle," primordial matter</note>, take 3 measures of sal ammoniac, thrice sublimated, and 3 quarters. Grind all these together at once, mix them, and grind them upon a round marble stone with "resuated" oil <note>likely a distilled or resinous oil</note> until it is made like a thick paste. And so let it be allowed to dry in the sun, or over a slow fire in a glass vessel. And when it has been well dried, let it be ground a second time as before, and let it be dried; and once dried, let it be dissolved with the said oil so that it is like a clear sauce. And thus placed in a glass vessel, let it be set to dissolve and digest under horse manure <note>a common alchemical method for maintaining a steady, gentle heat</note> in continuous heat for seven days or more. Then, once extracted, it will be coagulated among hot ashes. Let the "thirdings" <note>triple repetitions</note>, grindings, soakings, and dryings be repeated until the dried metals, when spread upon an ignited iron plate, flow like wax. Otherwise, let the sublimations be repeated as before, until in its fusion or entry upon the aforementioned body or plate it does not smoke, but confirms its fixation with its rotation, and the whole enters manifestly without smoke. Then it will be incomparably more precious than gold and silver. One part of this converts four parts of prepared moon <note>alchemical symbol for silver</note> into true sun <note>alchemical symbol for gold</note>.

### On the names of the seven planets which are assigned to the seven metals

### On the Four Principal Spirits

There are four principal spirits: Orpiment <note>original: "Auripigmentū"; a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, Sulfur, Quicksilver <note>original: "Argentū viuū"; mercury</note>, and Sal Ammoniac <note>original: "Sal ammoniacū"; ammonium chloride</note>. These are sometimes called "angels," sometimes "accidents," and sometimes "fates." From these, our histories <note>likely referring to alchemical accounts or processes</note> derive many things for themselves.

Some parts are essential, while many others are secondary.

The principal parts, therefore, are the four spirits and the seven bodies <note>the seven metals associated with the planets</note>.

The spirits are these: <unclear>bz</unclear> Quicksilver, Salt <note>likely a scribal error or specific salt variant</note>, Orpiment or Arsenic, and Sulfur.

The seven bodies are Gold, Silver, Iron, Copper, Tin, Lead, and Brass <note>original: "auricalcū"; orichalcum</note>.

The secondary parts, however, are Feathered Alum, Glass Alum, Alkali Salt, Rock Salt <note>original: "Sal gemie"</note>, Saltpeter, Lime of Tartar, and Vitriol <note>original: "Coporosa"</note>, Butyrum <note>likely "butter" of a metal or a fatty substance</note>, urine of boys, Vinegar, "Capitellum" <note>a strong lye</note>, Quicklime, soap, and other sharp, astringent, and penetrating things.

<margin>On the spirits that tint and color the bodies.</margin>
It must be noted, therefore, that spirits tint and color the bodies. But they do not do so unless they have been prepared as is required. Furthermore, the bodies do not receive the tincture unless they have first been well-purged of their infirmities. This is done by calcining <note>heating to a high temperature to reduce to powder</note> each one or by washing them well with sharp waters <note>acids</note>.

<margin>On the preparation of spirits.</margin>
Note that spirits are prepared by purging or sublimating <note>the process of turning a solid into vapor and back to solid to purify it</note>, macerating and congealing, dissolving and fermenting. And thus bodies are made spiritual and spirits are made into bodies, which is the goal of this art.

<column-break/>

### On the Sublimation of Quicksilver

The preparation of Quicksilver is done briefly and very well with salts in a stone mortar; afterwards, it should be immediately separated from the salts with hot water. Then let it be sublimated in this manner by the strength of the writings.

Take half a pound <note>original: "lib. S." for libra semis</note> of Roman Vitriol or copperas and half a pound of glass alum; melt these, having been pulverized, in a lead-glazed earthen pan. Once melted, add half a pound of Quicksilver, stirring continually with a stick until it is broken down and hardened. Then, place the pulverized mixture in a sublimation vessel well-sealed with "lute of wisdom" <note>original: "luto sapie"; a specialized airtight alchemical clay</note> and covered with earth, and let the sublimation be performed sufficiently.

### On the Sublimation of Sal Ammoniac

This is the sublimation of Sal Ammoniac. Take half a pound of Rock Salt, half a pound of common salt, and half a pound of Sal Ammoniac. Grind these together on a porphyry stone and sublimate them only twice, which is enough and suffices.

### On the Sublimation of Orpiment

This is the sublimation of Orpiment. First, boil the pulverized material for an hour in vinegar or the skimmed urine of a young boy so that its oiliness and fiery wind <note>volatile impurities</note> may be removed. It must boil until it is well thickened and hardened. After this, take half a pound of burnt copper <note>original: "eris usum"</note>, half a pound of ceruse <note>white lead</note>, and one pound of Orpiment prepared as already described. Incorporate these together by grinding on a marble stone and sublimate three times.
